narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='c1'/>Put k as one in the first claim. Two times three take away four is two, so it is always two.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>One number that works does not prove always. Try k as two.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>Three times four take away five is seven, not two.

narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>To check a false claim, show one number where it fails.
<bookmark mark='k2'/>For the true claim, test a few odd squares. Nine, twenty five and forty nine are each one more than a multiple of eight.

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu puts k as one, gets two, and says it is always two. With k as two the expression gives seven, so one case proves nothing.
